question.text: The sponsor-commitment (skin-in-the-game) requirement for a Cat III AIF is:

answer.text: 2.5% of corpus or INR 5 crore, whichever is lower
5% of corpus or INR 10 crore, whichever is lower
10% of corpus with no absolute cap
Nil — sponsor commitment is voluntary for Cat III

explanation.text: The Logic: Cat III sponsors must commit 5% of the corpus or INR 10 crore, whichever is LOWER. This is a higher quantum than Cat I/II's 2.5% / INR 5 crore. The skin-in-the-game rule aligns manager/sponsor interest with investors. The Trap: Option A is Cat I/II's rule — the classic Cat I/II vs Cat III swap trap. Option C is overstated; option D is wrong, commitment is mandatory. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-D's Cat I/II manager exam tests 2.5%/INR 5 cr; XIX-E tests 5%/INR 10 cr for Cat III. Don't swap them. Manager's Pro-Tip: If your corpus is INR 400 cr, 5% = INR 20 cr but cap at INR 10 cr — so you commit INR 10 cr. Budget this at fund launch and carve a sponsor entity if the management company cannot fund it.
